primary_motivation.title: Opponent Modeling in Stratego
primary_motivation.author: J. A. Stankiewicz
primary_motivation.transfer: Use observed public behavior to update hidden-rank beliefs, with positive support for bluffs. This pilot fits categorical public-history feature likelihoods on our own development games; it does not reproduce the paper's human database or complete opponent model.

related_evidence.title: Scalable Decision Making for Games of Imperfect Information
related_evidence.transfer: Learned beliefs and constrained policy improvement are successful components of a full Classic Stratego system. This experiment isolates belief changes and leaves constrained search for a separate test.

related_evidence.title: Mastering the Game of Stratego with Model-Free Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
related_evidence.transfer: Information asymmetry includes both discovery and secrecy; improved prediction alone need not translate into stronger decisions.

implemented_features: owner-normalized origin row and symmetric file
last approach to a disclosed opposing rank
last retreat from a disclosed opposing rank
implementation: Separate moved/unmoved categorical tables; empirical marginal smoothing with pseudocount 10; soft likelihood log bounds [-2,2]. Temperature selected from 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 by game-weighted calibration log loss. Exact inventory and masks constrain sequential sampling; proposal probabilities are importance-corrected. Eight worlds and four-ply masked continuation remain fixed.
limitations: A compact naive conditional feature model, not a full action-choice likelihood or learned neural policy. Fractional marginals are used for temperature calibration; actual eight-world and 256-world posterior predictions are evaluated separately. Sparse self-normalized sampling is noisy. No claim of optimal belief inference or guaranteed strength.
